items.title: Show HN: It's now easy to install Linux on an Android Phone – Android2linux
items.description:
Show HN: Hey HN! One of my biggest dreams (really) was to have a Linux phone. I tried to install on some phones in the past, even the ones that would be marked as compatible and it was always so difficult that I couldn't really do it. Yesterday I decided to try again, this time using Claude to do most of the work. A couple hours later it runs postmarketOS as my second phone: 4G, SMS, a terminal, SSH. It took two fixes. U-Boot didn't recognise my phone model, so I patched 14 bytes of its device-tree match strings. Then the modem wasn't working, because the packaged TFTP server that lends the modem a folder mishandled its file-size queries but an upstream build fixed it. The repo is what came out of it: guides for any phone (but specific just for my xiaomi), an agent skill that follows the same method and safety rules, notes per phone, and web apps reworked for a phone screen (WhatsApp Web for desktop with a one-pane layout). What doesn't work (in this phone of mine): no charger driver yet (slow charging), no cameras, and no banking apps, so I keep an Android at home for those. Whether this works for you depends on your phone having a port. reports through the issue forms help, especially for phones that don't work yet. I think that finally succeeding at having a Linux phone is worth creating a post on HN. I was thinking about a Tell HN but decided to convert the knowledge into a repo so more people can share, discuss, add their phones, new apps, etc. Hope it helps!
Website metadata: Turn an Android phone into a Linux pocket computer you control: guides, an agent skill, phone notes, scripts and apps for postmarketOS and Ubuntu Touch. - android2linux/android2linux

items.title: Show HN: Musset, open-source Scrivener alternative with an AI that never writes
items.description:
Show HN: I’m writing my first novel and could not find an app that fit my workflow: quiet like iA Writer, organized like Scrivener, and with AI so I can discuss my book while I write it. It allows me to feel less “alone” and have a sounding board while I write. - A book is a folder of plain Markdown files. Musset commits to a git repo, tracks versions and drafts without you having to know git. - Revisions are CriticMarkup inside the text. It manages docx revisions too, so your editor can edit a Word doc and you import their comments. - PDFs are typeset using Typst, embedded in the app, following each language’s typographic rules. - Spelling and grammar are checked using LanguageTool, also embedded. - Mac/Word, WordStar, vi and Emacs keyboard modes. The AI is optional and uses your Codex or Claude Code CLI. It comments, leaves margin notes, and checks continuity and your chapters against your style rules. It’s GPL-3.0 and free during the beta. When or if it reaches 1.0, if there is sufficient interest, the idea is to make it a small one-time payment ($9.90). There is a paid sync service (git hosting) that lets you share a book with beta readers and editors. Download: https://musset.app I’d love to have some feedback!
Website metadata: Open-source Mac app for writing novels and books: plain Markdown files, versions, typeset PDF and EPUB. A native Scrivener and Ulysses alternative, with an AI editor that never writes for you. - Musset-App/musset
items.product_description: Open-source Mac app for writing novels and books: plain Markdown files, versions, typeset PDF and EPUB. A native Scrivener and Ulysses alternative, with an AI editor that never writes for you. - Musset-App/musset

items.title: Show HN: Lightweight FUSE-based encrypted, compressed filesystem for Linux
items.description:
Show HN: A personal project for digging deeper into Linux system programming, ObFUSEcate implements a file backed virtual block device that automatically performs compression and encryption as blocks are accessed. This virtual device can be mounted via FUSE (requiring no root privileges) to provide, effectively, a "live" compressed, encrypted archive. Written in C++, and intended to have minimal dependencies, it has custom 32 bit arithmetic encoding/decoding, ChaCha20-Poly1305 authenticated encryption, and CRC8 + XOR parity error-correction.

items.description:
Show HN: Hi everyone, Board is a way to create, deploy, and fund a trading bot in 10 seconds. My co-founders and I built Board out of our own necessity. Every time we had a new trading strategy, we would need to manually input it into our broker accounts and monitor the situation ourselves. We looked at all of our trading strategies over the past 3 years and added everything to the board that would be required to rebuild them from scratch. Now, when we have a new strategy, we chat with AI to create the strategy. We review the board to confirm that it matches what we expect, and we deploy it. We don't have to worry about setting up webhooks for signals or keeping it running on our computer locally. The whole system is built on top of tokenized stocks and commodities. You always have access to withdraw your funds.

items.title: Show HN: OpenComputer – an open source alternative to Devin
items.description:
Show HN: Hi HN! Utpal here, I'm one of the founders of OpenComputer. OpenComputer is an open source cloud coding agent for teams that can run in your own cloud account (AWS, GCP, Azure). We run the agent harness and the sandbox on the same durable VM (architecture in the docs [1]). First commit lands in 24s; the alternatives we benchmarked took 53-72s (benchmarks below [2]). Two other choices: - One VM per team, scalable horizontally. Sessions are isolated in git worktrees. - Session files are backed up to a repo after every turn, so any session can resume on another VM. We noticed that past ~640 session-hours a month, one always-on 4 vCPU VM is cheaper than per-session E2B sandboxes, for example. So at scale, this setup would not only be faster than current SOTA coding agents, but also more cost-efficient. Feel free to try via cloud for free [4] or self host. We would love any and all feedback, and happy to answer any questions! Full demo below [3]. [1]: https://docs.opencomputer.dev/getting-started/architecture [2]: https://opencomputer.dev/blog/cloud-agents-as-fast-as-local/ [3]: https://x.com/IgorZIJ/status/2121309785882591711 [4]: https://app.opencomputer.dev

items.title: Show HN: ArkViz – AI generated software architecture diagrams
items.description:
Show HN: Hi HN, I’m Bryant, founder of ArkViz ( https://arkviz.io ). ArkViz is a product to automatically generate architecture diagrams from your codebase using AI. The vision behind ArkViz is to supercharge both AI agents and humans by providing AI agents deeper relational context using structured model diagram formats, and by providing humans with a rich visual representation you can interact with, with features like zooming, panning, search, and show composing files. In this new age of AI, you can generate a structured model diagram from your codebase in seconds, quicker and better than a human. Not only can the generated diagram be a visual documentation tool for humans, AI agents can also benefit from the context of a pre-generated architecture diagram that lives alongside a project’s codebase. This concept has already been proven by context files like CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, ARCHITECTURE.md living in the root of your repository. The differentiator between ARCHITECTURE.md and ArkViz is that ArkViz generates a structured model diagram of the system, while ARCHITECTURE.md is broader in scope and purely text. ArkViz aims to be a supplement to ARCHITECTURE.md to provide deeper understanding like how components are connected, which components live inside other components, which files compose a component. — Why ArkViz? Software engineering teams often create diagrams to aid in the documentation of their software systems. They are incredibly useful for onboarding new engineers and understanding projects. However, they take time to create and maintain, so are often non-existent or out of date. ArkViz automates the creation and maintenance of software architecture diagrams, seamlessly and securely. AI agents thrive when they have high quality context, including for architecture diagrams. However not all diagram formats out there are optimized for AI. A diagram showing connected systems and components can be represented in essentially 3 ways: 1. Unstructured drawing / canvas format (e.g. draw.io, Excalidraw, Figma, LucidChart) - Quick to get started but hard to maintain. - Good for brainstorming and whiteboarding - The format carries no semantic meaning and is basically represented by pixels, shapes, and vectors. Positioning is stored - Passing this to an AI agent as context has questionable value. 2. Structured diagramming formats (e.g. Mermaid, d2lang) - A level of abstraction higher than a 2D drawing canvas - Good for quick isolated diagram, like on GitHub - Represent
Website metadata: Generate beautiful, always up-to-date architecture diagrams of your software projects from all your data sources. Powered by AI.

items.title: Show HN: LarpLess, open-source study tracker detecting distractions locally
items.description:
Show HN: I am ashamed to admit that I am one of those students who go to the library and get very little done (a.k.a. larping). It's very easy to get distracted if you have any electronic devices with you, but as a CS major, I can't just switch to pen and paper. That's why I started building this app called LarpLess with the help of a few friends. LarpLess is a macOS/Windows app that checks your screen and camera with local AI to determine what you are studying or if you are distracted. Gives you a focus percentage at the end, with a breakdown of what you did during your session (Math, Physics, etc.) Privacy is a big concern for an app like this, so it is open-source (AGPL 3.0) and uses locally run open-source models. It doesn't connect to the internet unless you want to check for updates or enable the friends feature (Disabled by default. You can make an account, add friends and see their shared study sessions/share your study sessions). For the camera, it uses an object detection model, YOLO11n, to detect if there is a person and/or a phone at 1fps. For the screen, there are 2 options: the one we did first is reading window titles + a VLM on Ollama (default is qwen3-vl:2b), simple but power/RAM hungry. The one my friend added later can run on an average laptop easily. It takes less than a second for a verdict. It scores window titles + OCR text on the screen with MiniLM text embeddings and scores the screenshot with image embeddings using SigLIP 2. SigLIP 2 decides if the user is distracted, and MiniLM decides what they are working on. You can run the classifier-based mode on any modern laptop. If you want to use the VLM mode, you need a good GPU with enough VRAM (3GB+) to hold the model in it. You can try it out by downloading the macOS version from GitHub ( https://github.com/AlperErg/larpless/releases ) or the Windows version from the Microsoft Store ( https://apps.microsoft.com/detail/9nrvvphtmr9x ). I found it helpful for studying. I hope that you will as well. I'd appreciate it if you can give it a go and kindly share your thoughts. p.s. My friend, who also works on this with me, posted about it before but without a description and not on Show HN, so I decided to post on Show HN with a good description.

I've even got support from a Sim racing guy and built a web driver so he gets full force feedback for his rig, and it works. Anyway, just a bit of fun! Uses LIDAR data from the UK Gov + OpenStreetMap data to build the world. Technically, I could do the whole of England/Wales...but the data storage would be huge!
